subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — Lumina workload details and clarifying questions
messages:
From: Elliot Tan <elliot@lumina.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@lumina.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — workload data attached

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — Lumina is keen to get an initial sizing estimate for a dedicated Redwood deployment so we can include it in our infrastructure budget and procurement timeline. I've attached a small sample of request logs and some traffic summaries. Our immediate ask: a high-level GPU estimate (type + count) and whether Redwood would recommend a single dedicated pool or split pools for burst vs baseline traffic.

Quick background:
- Primary use case: conversational agents and short-form summarization for enterprise customers (no PII).
- Expected daily active users in pilot: ~60k (in month 1).
- Peak concurrent chats (typical spike): ~6k concurrent sessions; each session averages 1.8 requests/sec during active typing bursts.
- Preferred model family: Llama 3 70B (we're open to quantized variants).

Attached: lumina_workload_sample_logs.json (snippet) and a one-page traffic summary. Could you send your dedicated sizing questionnaire or template so our infra team can fill out anything more detailed you need? Also include any suggestions around acceptable prompt/response token budgets for cost planning.

Best,
Elliot Tan
Head of ML Platform, Lumina AI
E: elliot@lumina.ai

Attachment: lumina_workload_sample_logs.json (json, 324 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Tan <elliot@lumina.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — workload data attached

Hi Elliot — thanks for the data and context, this is exactly what we need to start a sizing pass. I've attached our dedicated sizing template (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx) — it covers traffic profiles, concurrency buckets, prompt/response token distributions, session vs batch inference, and SLA/latency targets. A few clarifying questions before we hand this to your infra/ML ops team: 

1) For the 6k concurrent sessions peak: is that steady for multiple hours or short spikes (<= 5 min)?
2) Average prompt length vs expected response length (tokens) — your logs hint at short prompts but please confirm P50/P95/Max token sizes.
3) Do you need embeddings + generation from the same pool, or can embeddings go to a separate, cheaper pool?
4) Any regulatory or network constraints for a dedicated VPC deployment (e.g., egress restrictions)?

If you prefer, Jonas (solutions) can run a quick counter-proposal with a 2-tier pool design: baseline reserved capacity + burst autoscale. I'll leave him on this thread to add technical constraints.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Tan <elliot@lumina.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — workload data attached

Elliot — quick technical notes / assumptions I'm going to use for an initial GPU estimate: 

- Model & config: Llama 3 70B quantized to int8 (with KV-cache). If you require FP16 or int4, call that out — int8 is our usual cost/latency sweet spot for 70B.
- Typical tokens: assume P50 prompt = 45 tokens, P95 prompt = 220 tokens; P50 response = 110 tokens, P95 response = 650 tokens. Please correct these if your logs show otherwise.
- Latency SLO: are you targeting <300 ms P95 per token (interactive) or are longer latencies acceptable?
- Concurrency modeling: 6k concurrent sessions * 1.8 rps during typing bursts => ~10.8k tokens/sec entering system if each request ~1 token per rps equivalent. Realistic conversion: multiply requests/sec by average (prompt+response) token size to compute token/sec.

Initial sizing heuristic (very rough):
- Baseline reserved pool for steady-state: sized for 2k concurrent interactive users at baseline activity (about 2.5 average rps equivalent across the pool) — estimate 8 x A100-80GB equiv for baseline (quantized runtime).
- Burst/autoscale pool for peak traffic: additional 12 x A100-80GB equiv as burst headroom; this allows for 6k peak with headroom for QA and retries.

I'll produce a more precise number once we have token distributions and the filled spreadsheet. Also: confirm whether embeddings queries are latency-sensitive — they can usually be offloaded to cheaper T4/RTX pools if throughput is the main constraint.

— Jonas
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Tan <elliot@lumina.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, procurement@lumina.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — workload data attached

Thanks Soojin / Jonas — answering the clarifying questions and filling the high level fields here (we'll return the completed spreadsheet by EOD).

1) Peak spike shape: typically short bursts (3–8 minutes) correlated with business hours and product releases. Spikes occur multiple times per day but not sustained for >20 minutes.
2) Token distributions (approx, from the attached sample logs): P50 prompt = 34 tokens, P95 prompt = 180 tokens, Max prompt observed = 2,100 tokens (rare). P50 response = 96 tokens, P95 response = 520 tokens, Max response = 3,400 tokens (long-form summarization).
3) Embeddings: separate pipeline; not latency-critical for our use case. Prefer to run embeddings on a cheaper, separate pool.
4) VPC: yes, we require VPC + customer-managed KMS. No unusual egress rules beyond standard enterprise firewall.

Other constraints:
- We need a plan for model rollouts (canary and rollback) and a fast fallback to a smaller Llama 3 13B if the 70B pool is temporarily degraded.
- Cost target: keep token-serving unit economics below $0.0009 per generated token in steady-state (guideline, negotiable).

I'll upload the completed sheet and a 48-hour sample log later today (attached). Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Elliot

Attachment: lumina_workload_sample_logs_v2.json (json, 1.1 MB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Tan <elliot@lumina.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 18:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — workload data attached

Elliot — perfect, that token distribution is very helpful. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Jonas will produce a short proposal (GPU types & counts, lane architecture: reserved baseline + burst autoscale, and fallback policies) by EOD tomorrow, using the P50/P95 numbers you provided. We'll include expected throughput (tokens/sec) calculations and a cost range for steady-state vs peak.
2) We'll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW template for dedicated capacity (SLA, VPC/KMS responsibilities, support tiers) and share it with your procurement contact. Marissa — can you own the procurement path and pricing cadence for this deal?

Marissa: ball in your court for pricing / discounts tied to a 12-month commit. Elliot: once we have the completed spreadsheet, Jonas will slot realistic hardware counts; if you need a workshop with your infra team, we can set that up next week.

Thanks — looking forward to the completed sheet.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
